correctness.rationale: Weyl-unitary basis expansion proves the exact squared projection formula. Charlier recurrence and exact derivative identity show all local maxima at Laguerre roots. Fixed-degree Charlier generating-function limits plus explicit exponential Poisson-tail bounds imply global convergence. Hermite derivative factorization and strictly decreasing Sonin energy at positive zeros give the global parity law. CHECK.py ran and independently corroborated 42 exact identities, all local candidate counts for six orders, 18 local limits, 36 coefficient comparisons and 45 derivative samples. The computation is not used as an infinite proof.

evidence: Charlier polynomial/Hermite transition is established in Nilsson, Theorem 1, https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00365-021-09559-w .
The limiting polynomial sum is the Hermite Christoffel diagonal, equal up to normalization to the GUE one-point density; this identity is classical.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The new Fock projection problem is mathematically equivalent, in its fixed-order asymptotic limit, to maximizing a finite Hermite Christoffel diagonal; its finite-degree stationarity is equivalent to an associated-Laguerre zero condition. Neither the Charlier transition nor the Christoffel identity alone states the single-site optimum or proves the global parity rule. A known GUE-density optimizer theorem under a different name would reduce priority, so this equivalence is not hidden.

originality.rationale: The claim is a finite- and asymptotic sharp Fock single-site k-jet design for all fixed k>=2. Existing derivative density theorems, Charlier limits, Hermite kernel identities and the known first-jet special case do not directly state or imply the all-order finite Laguerre stationary classification together with the parity-dependent global optimizer. Acknowledged priority risk remains for equivalent Hermite density or displaced-state formulations.
residual_risks: Random-matrix theory may contain the identical global Hermite one-point-density maximizer parity classification under different terminology; searches did not conclusively exclude it.
Displaced number-state quantum optics may formulate equivalent finite associated-Laguerre optimization.
Only relevant sections of primary texts were materially examined; search absence is not proof of uniqueness, and no independent peer validation was conducted.

value.rationale: The single-site value-plus-jet approximation is a natural finite Hermite sampling primitive. It has an exact k+1-element optimizer-candidate reduction for any N>k, and a sharp asymptotic value and complete parity classification for every fixed order k>=2. The alternating center/off-center optimizer geometry changes by the full sqrt(N) scale and provides actionable site placement and Hermite-augmented Fock/Gabor stability benchmarks; it is not merely an arbitrary special-function evaluation.
